title: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed Table S1.xlsx, 'core and sample ID.xlsx' and 'sample ID cohort 2.xlsx' from Zenodo 22675354 (CC-BY-4.0). Table S1: 150 tumour samples (138 cohort 1 + 12 cohort 2; 92 IS (immunosuppressed) / 58 IC (immunocompetent); 118 SCC, 32 BCC), 138-row follow-up sheet (32 recurrences, 48 deaths), 54-row Cleveland Clinic validation cohort (29 IS / 25 IC). Core map: 189 TMA (tissue microarray) cores across 3 TMAs. Listed Zenodo files (H&E .tif 0.4-5 GB each, mIF .qptiff 2.5-7.5 GB, Xenium zip 8.8 GB) and GEO file lists: GSE316922 scRNA-seq 3.4 GB (36 samples), GSE318638 scTCR 29 MB (34), GSE308361 spatial ATAC/multiome 46.6 GB, GSE306130 Xenium, GSE306129 spatial ATAC.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paywalled, no PMC full text). Cell-type annotations, macrophage-state definitions and niche calls were not opened; they are not deposited as a simple table that I could find.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: Zenodo records are open CC-BY-4.0; GEO series public since 2026-08-07.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified: the only measured labels are patient-level (Immune_Status IS/IC, recurrence, survival) in Table S1. Any per-cell or per-spot label (macrophage state, niche) would have to be constructed by clustering the omics data.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified in file listings: H&E images, mIF images, count matrices (MTX) and TCR contig CSVs are deposited, though mostly as multi-GB files.

a4_units_stated.note: Labels are categorical; counts are standard 10x formats (from file names only).

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified: the honest unit is the patient/tumour: 150 samples in Table S1 (92 IS / 58 IC), 189 TMA cores, ~36 scRNA-seq samples, plus 54 external cases. Far below the ~400 needed for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: H&E slides 0.4-5 GB each (~23 GB for cohort 2+TMAs); mIF ~40 GB; spatial ATAC 46.6 GB; scRNA 3.4 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Image-based prediction of immune status needs tens of GB of whole-slide images and GPU-scale feature extraction.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable against full text (paywalled); Table S1 sample counts are internally consistent with the core map.

a8_label_provenance.note: Immune status is clinical history (transplant, CLL etc.), a real measurement, not a model output.

backbone.name: UNI or CONCH (pathology image foundation models) for H&E; scGPT for single cells
backbone.hardware: GPU realistically needed for whole-slide tiling

controls.external_validation: Cleveland Clinic cohort (54 cSCC cases) in Table S1

honest_claim_h3: At best: H&E or mIF features separate immunosuppressed from immunocompetent skin tumours among ~150 head-and-neck-dominated cases from one centre, validated on 54 cases from a second centre.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour tissue images to predict whether a skin-cancer patient is immunosuppressed or likely to recur.
plain_idea.train_on: Stained tissue images (H&E or multiplex immunofluorescence) of 150 tumour samples / 189 tissue-array cores, verified in the sample tables.
plain_idea.predict: Immunosuppressed versus immunocompetent status, or recurrence, taken from the clinical records in Table S1.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Dermatopathologists could flag high-risk tumours from routine slides, but 150 patients and multi-GB images make this an underpowered, GPU-heavy project.

ml_idea: Considered: slide-level classifier of immune status or recurrence from frozen pathology-foundation-model embeddings. Rejected: 150 patients, labels only at patient level, image working set tens of GB.

effort.compute_note: Sizes read from Zenodo/GEO file listings; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count patients with a usable label: done, 150 (92 IS/58 IC) — fails A5.

verdict_reason: A5/A2: the labelled unit is the patient (150 samples in Table S1, 54 external); per-cell states would have to be constructed by clustering, and the image data is tens of GB needing a GPU.
